description: The INFORM Risk Index is a global, open-source risk assessment for humanitarian crises and disasters, intended to support decisions on prevention, preparedness and response. It is produced by INFORM, a multi-stakeholder forum founded in 2014 by the Inter-Agency Standing Committee and the European Commission and guided by a steering group of UN agencies and partners, with the European Commission's Joint Research Centre as scientific lead. The index combines three dimensions, hazard and exposure, vulnerability, and lack of coping capacity, each built from open indicators, into country scores and ranks; related products are INFORM Subnational Risk models for regions and countries, the INFORM Severity Index of ongoing crises and INFORM Climate Change, which applies climate and socioeconomic projections, with INFORM Warning in development. Results are released twice a year (the Mid 2026 edition is current) and downloaded free of charge as spreadsheets after a short survey; the terms of use were not stated on the page read. Caveats: national averages hide local variation, indicators lag by years, and the index measures humanitarian risk, not infrastructure performance. It is used as social vulnerability and coping capacity context in multi-hazard risk and resilience studies of infrastructure, for prioritising climate adaptation and emergency response, and complements EM-DAT event data and ThinkHazard hazard levels.
